investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because agent creation never progressed past the scheduling phase.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes, and the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never returned a VM-backed agent, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) unpopulated and causing the eval to fail. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect, and is scoped to the eval's production-api runtime environment. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact beyond the observability eval is unconfirmed.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: pod remained unscheduled for 135s before the check ended at 2026-07-03T07:39:34.415Z with status=fail and latencyMs=138576.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector') with pod stuck for 148s, confirming the condition persisted across sequential eval runs.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same scheduler error with pod stuck for 141s, further confirming sustained capacity exhaustion.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in ['running','idle','ready'], neither of which can be satisfied without a running pod.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — no capacity remains for new peer-pod VMs, and preemption found no evictable victims, confirming all slots are occupied by running workloads.

[High confidence] The 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector configuration, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible for remote-agent pods; any saturation of those 2 nodes causes a total scheduling blackout.

[Medium confidence] A concurrent workload spike or a previously created remote-agent pod that was not cleaned up may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new probe pods from being scheduled.
[Low confidence] A misconfiguration in the node affinity/selector rules could be incorrectly excluding nodes that should be eligible, artificially shrinking the schedulable pool to 2 nodes.

Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so the remote-agent-state probe produced zero evidence — all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes. Every new remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was rejected as Unschedulable (0/6 nodes available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector), and preemption could not free capacity. Because pod scheduling is a prerequisite for VM readiness and agent lifecycle, the eval runner's createAgent step (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never produced a live agent, causing the remote-agent-state probe to return no evidence and fail its expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure scoped to the remote-agent swarm node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata/PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata.peerpods.io VM pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was returned because agent creation never completed — the pod never left the Unschedulable state. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes cluster capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. When the eval runner called createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the scheduler reported "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and preemption found no victims. The pod remained Unschedulable for 141 s (remote-agent-runtime), 135 s (remote-agent-create), and 148 s (remote-agent-state) before each check timed out. Because the agent pod never started, the probe returned no evidence, violating all five required-evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 266–269.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent eval runs, other workloads, or leaked/stuck pods from prior eval runs may have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for new agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already small and any contention exhausts it quickly.

Tertiary — eval cleanup failure leaving orphaned remote-agent pods: if a prior eval run's withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) did not complete successfully, previously allocated kata.peerpods.io/vm slots may not have been released, reducing available capacity for subsequent runs.

Lower confidence — transient cluster scaling lag: the kata.peerpods.io node pool may not have auto-scaled in time to absorb the eval's demand, particularly if multiple checks ran in close succession (remote-agent-create ended at 07:39:34, remote-agent-state ended at 07:42:10, remote-agent-runtime ended at 07:44:38).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because agent creation never progressed past the scheduling phase.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes, and the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never returned a VM-backed agent, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) unpopulated and causing the eval to fail. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect, and is scoped to the eval's production-api runtime environment. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact beyond the observability eval is unconfirmed.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same scheduler error with pod stuck for 141s, further confirming sustained capacity exhaustion.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in ['running','idle','ready'], neither of which can be satisfied without a running pod.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — no capacity remains for new peer-pod VMs, and preemption found no evictable victims, confirming all slots are occupied by running workloads.

[High confidence] The 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector configuration, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible for remote-agent pods; any saturation of those 2 nodes causes a total scheduling blackout.

[Medium confidence] A concurrent workload spike or a previously created remote-agent pod that was not cleaned up may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new probe pods from being scheduled.
[Low confidence] A misconfiguration in the node affinity/selector rules could be incorrectly excluding nodes that should be eligible, artificially shrinking the schedulable pool to 2 nodes.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place agent pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so the remote-agent-state probe produced zero evidence — all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes. Every new remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was rejected as Unschedulable (0/6 nodes available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector), and preemption could not free capacity. Because pod scheduling is a prerequisite for VM readiness and agent lifecycle, the eval runner's createAgent step (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never produced a live agent, causing the remote-agent-state probe to return no evidence and fail its expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure scoped to the remote-agent swarm node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata/PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata.peerpods.io VM pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was returned because agent creation never completed — the pod never left the Unschedulable state. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes cluster capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. When the eval runner called createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the scheduler reported "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and preemption found no victims. The pod remained Unschedulable for 141 s (remote-agent-runtime), 135 s (remote-agent-create), and 148 s (remote-agent-state) before each check timed out. Because the agent pod never started, the probe returned no evidence, violating all five required-evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 266–269.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' and 'No preemption victims found' — pod was Unschedulable for 141 s on remote-agent-runtime.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=148087, status=fail, endedAt=2026-07-03T07:44:38.331Z — check ran to timeout without producing any evidence.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message was captured.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing, matching the contract defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 266–269 (source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270).
sibling.remote-agent-create: same scheduler error, pod Unschedulable for 135 s, empty evidence — confirms the failure is not isolated to the runtime check.
sibling.remote-agent-state: same scheduler error, pod Unschedulable for 148 s, empty evidence — confirms the failure spans the full remote-agent lifecycle sequence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which is the call that triggers remote VM pod scheduling; failure at this step prevents all downstream evidence collection.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:185: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the observed latency of 148087 ms is well within the outage threshold, confirming the check timed out on scheduling, not on a latency breach.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent eval runs, other workloads, or leaked/stuck pods from prior eval runs may have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for new agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already small and any contention exhausts it quickly.

Tertiary — eval cleanup failure leaving orphaned remote-agent pods: if a prior eval run's withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) did not complete successfully, previously allocated kata.peerpods.io/vm slots may not have been released, reducing available capacity for subsequent runs.

Lower confidence — transient cluster scaling lag: the kata.peerpods.io node pool may not have auto-scaled in time to absorb the eval's demand, particularly if multiple checks ran in close succession (remote-agent-create ended at 07:39:34, remote-agent-state ended at 07:42:10, remote-agent-runtime ended at 07:44:38).

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in the production-api cluster to determine current VM slot utilization and identify any pods holding slots from prior eval runs.
Check for orphaned remote-agent pods that may not have been cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs; terminate any stuck pods to free VM slots.

Determine whether the node affinity/selector configuration intentionally restricts remote-agent pods to only 2 of 6 nodes; if so, evaluate whether additional nodes should be labeled to expand the scheduling pool.
Re-run the three remote-agent eval checks after confirming or restoring VM slot availability to verify the feature health status recovers.

Consider adding a pre-flight check in the eval runner that verifies kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available before attempting agent creation, to produce a more actionable SKIP or WARN result instead of a timeout-driven FAIL.

Review whether the eval run cadence (staleAfterMinutes=20 for all three checks) combined with sequential check execution could cause self-contention on the limited VM pool, and whether staggering or serializing remote-agent checks would reduce scheduling pressure.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes show ample free capacity at the time of the failure, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a misconfigured node selector or affinity rule would become the primary hypothesis.

If no other pods were consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots during the failure window, the cause is more likely a node affinity/selector misconfiguration that permanently excludes all 6 nodes rather than transient exhaustion.
If a subsequent eval run immediately after this failure succeeds without any cluster changes, the failure was a transient scheduling spike rather than a persistent capacity problem.
If the remote-agent-create check had passed while remote-agent-runtime failed, the root cause would be localized to the runtime step rather than the shared VM scheduling layer.
If the withCleanup function is confirmed to have run successfully on all prior eval runs (no orphaned pods), cleanup leakage is not a contributing factor.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check (e.g., remote-agent-vm-capacity) that queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested ratio on eligible nodes and warns when utilization exceeds a threshold, before any agent creation is attempted.
Add a cleanup-verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote-agent pods remain after each eval run cycle, catching withCleanup failures before they accumulate into capacity exhaustion.

Add a node-affinity-coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector meets a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 3 nodes), alerting when the eligible pool shrinks below a safe level.
Consider a retry-with-backoff eval variant for remote-agent-create that distinguishes between a transient scheduling delay and a persistent Unschedulable state, enabling finer-grained alerting.
